 Statement from Nebraska Head Football Coach Matt Rhule: 
 "Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season. As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program—including wins and losses—and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted.
 "While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working. Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties. As I have recently shared, Dana has a fantastic offensive mind, he is a strong leader, and he has done great work here at Nebraska. But simply, we need a change. Co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas will take over play-calling duties.
 "I will continue to evaluate our program through the season and certainly at its conclusion and make additional changes where I believe they will help us win.
 "The Nebraska fan base has high expectations and I embrace them, and I also know of their passionate support of the young men in our program. I hope they will continue to be there for our players with very important games still ahead. Our entire program is determined to finish this season strong."
 I think every fan that has sat through the past four games knew something had to change. Matt Rhule's seat is getting warm and it is no surprise that he made a move. Holgorsen seemed like a home-run hire when Matt Rhule brought him to Lincoln but we've seen that side of the ball struggle mightily.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Now, we move on to the Glenn Thomas era of Husker offense.
 Go Big Red.
